topics.topic: Allowed service base URLs and operation-path joining
questions: Which exact base-URL forms are valid, and precisely how is the operation path joined to a base URL that already contains path or delimiter components?

Are userinfo, query, fragment, non-root path prefixes, repeated trailing slashes, encoded delimiters and noncanonical host or port forms allowed, and exactly how are they joined and represented in the `Host` header?

Are user information, an existing path, query, fragment, percent-encoded authority components, IPv6 zone identifiers and non-default ports permitted in `api_base_url`, and how is the declared path joined when any are present?

judgement.why: This is the same base-URL grammar and path-joining question previously assigned to State 6.

precedent.topic: Allowed api_base_url components and exact path-joining normalization
precedent.why: The accepted base-URL grammar, joining rules and Host serialization are format and encoding details belonging to State 6.

topics.topic: Filesystem ownership, permissions, links, and contents required for private storage
questions: What exact filesystem ownership and permission checks define a private data directory and private contents?
What exact owner, file-type and permission-bit checks define `private`, and are parent directories, hard links and newly created entries included?
What exact ownership, permission-bit and ACL conditions make the directory, its subdirectories and files ‘private,’ and are unexpected hard links or files grounds for refusal?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged private-data-directory filesystem question judged previously.

precedent.topic: Ownership, permissions, existence, and creation policy for the data directory and its files
quotes:
The directory and everything in it
   are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise.
precedent.why: The exact meaning of private filesystem state was already unspecified in this unchanged passage.

topics.topic: Handling of untrapped nondeterminism in sandboxed execution
questions: What additional restriction or qualification makes deterministic execution and deterministic admission enforceable?
What prevents or classifies nondeterministic outputs obtained through allowed Python and operating-system observations not in the trap list?
What happens when code uses an untrapped nondeterministic source available in Python, such as process identity, object identity, filesystem metadata or another standard-library clock/randomness path?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about determinism and untrapped nondeterministic sources.

precedent.topic: Required determinism and handling of untrapped nondeterministic sources
quotes: The same implementation on the same input yields the same output digest twice.
precedent.why: The determinism requirement and its enforcement question predated the change and were untouched by it.

topics.topic: Meaning and measurement unit of agent-visible failure-detail length
questions: Which length is disclosed for a non-open failure detail?
Is the reported length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points or characters after truncation, and is it the original or retained length?
Is the reported length measured in Unicode characters, UTF-8 bytes before truncation, UTF-8 bytes after truncation, or the original untruncated body/message length?

quotes: handle_get_repair_view: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] The class of a NodeExecution is the highest class among the items of its inputs, each SpooledFilesRef counting with its disclosure_class even when empty, and when its executed names a binding also of its outputs; the class of an operation execution's failure_detail is the highest of that class and the disclosure classes read_binding declares for that binding's outputs; the class of a TrialExecution is the highest class among its TrialCase's inputs (A07 rule 5, A09 rule 7); a failure_detail becomes DetailLength with its UTF-8 byte length and that class when the reader is an agent and the class is above open, and DetailText otherwise, always for the owner.
judgement.why: The later note specifies the UTF-8 byte length of the retained failure_detail.

topics.topic: Required and permitted trial-case input and expected-output fields
questions: Are missing and extra trial inputs refused, and when expected outputs are present must they cover exactly all output ports or may they be partial?
Must trial inputs name exactly every input port with no extras, and when expected outputs are present must they name exactly every output port or may they be partial?
When expected outputs are present, must they contain exactly every output port, or may they be partial; and are unknown or duplicate output names refused?

judgement.why: This is the same question about exact trial-case input and expected-output maps previously assigned to State 6 schemas.

precedent.topic: Required completeness and exact port sets for authored trial inputs and expected outputs
precedent.why: Required and optional request fields and the exact trial-case input and expected-output shapes belong to State 6 schemas.

topics.topic: Sandbox exchange protocol and function filesystem visibility
questions: How are inputs, outputs and trap reports transferred across the sandbox boundary, and what may untrusted code observe or modify in the exchange directory?
May function code inspect arbitrary runtime and exchange-directory files, or only the specific input artifacts exposed to that invocation?

May agent code itself read runtime files and create, enumerate or read arbitrary scratch files in the exchange directory, or are those paths accessible only to the runner for imports and input/output transfer?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about filesystem access available to sandboxed function code.

precedent.topic: Filesystem access available to sandboxed function code
quotes:
A function node runs one admitted implementation of one contract: declared input
in, declared output out, no network, no filesystem beyond its input, no clock, no
randomness, no secret, no service handle.
precedent.why: The filesystem restriction was unchanged, and the change did not alter sandbox path access.

topics.topic: Durable identification of the activation authorizing draft writes
questions: How does a run durably identify the exact FlowActivation that authorizes its draft-write sends, including after restart?
How is the exact FlowActivation identity recovered after the same version has been activated multiple times or later activations have replaced it?

quotes:
3. **Which FlowActivation a `draft-write` send names** (A10 rule 6): the latest
   FlowActivation of the run's pinned version before the Run record in store
   order — the one under which it started. `runs` finds it and passes it to
   `effects` with every call about one of the run's elements (State 3, "Facts
   passed down"); store order, not time, so two records never tie. A run's
   version was active when it started (A12 rule 1), so "none" cannot occur;
judgement.why: The later API text identifies the authorizing activation by its store position relative to the Run record.

topics.topic: Equality semantics for guard values
questions: Which equality relation decides a guard: canonical-JSON byte equality, JSON Schema enum equality, or host-language equality?
What exact equality decides guard activation and whether two guard values differ, including numbers such as `1` and `1.0` and structured closed values?

quotes: advance_run: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] The next node is the ready node with the smallest node_id; a node is ready when every input port holds its value: flow inputs delivered along every edge from them, constants to their port, and outputs of a concluded succeeded node along every edge whose guard is absent or whose guard port value equals the guard value as canonical JSON text. A mapped node, once selected, takes its elements in list order, executing every element with no concluded record that does not wait, before the next node is selected; a waiting or failed element does not stop the elements after it, and a concluded element is never executed again.
judgement.why: The later run contract defines guard equality as equality of canonical JSON text.

topics.topic: Media-type syntax, parsing, and response matching
questions: What exact media-type parser and validity rules decide whether a file response matches its port?
Which media-type forms are valid for ports, are parameters allowed, and how are invalid or injection-capable values refused?

judgement.why: Media-type grammar, parsing, header validity and serialization are format and field-constraint decisions belonging to State 6 or later.

topics.topic: Process-creation operations trapped versus limited by process count
questions: Which exact Python audit events and process-creation APIs count as `subprocess`, and is `fork` allowed until `process_count` is exhausted or immediately a `sandbox_violation`?
Which process-creation operations are trapped immediately as `sandbox_violation`, and which are allowed until `process_count` is exhausted?

quotes: execute_function: [BEHAVIOR] process_count bounds the tasks of the code alive at once: the runner's main thread counts as the first, every live thread and every process the code forked with os.fork counts with its threads, and bubblewrap's own processes are not counted, so process_count 1 allows code without threads or forks. Process creation other than os.fork — subprocess, os.system, os.posix_spawn, os.posix_spawnp and the os.exec family — is subprocess use and raises in the audit hook as a trap hit (A03 rule 4). The runner's audit hook, on os.fork and on starting a thread, counts the tasks of the environment's proc and, when the new task would exceed process_count, writes a resource hit to the channel and raises, so the execution concludes resource_exhausted even when the code catches the error; the parent's setrlimit, set above process_count by the tasks the runner and bubblewrap need, stays the outer bound, and a creation it refuses is reported the same way (A03 required test 2).
judgement.why: The later sandbox contract allows os.fork within the task bound and traps the listed alternative process-creation mechanisms as subprocess use.

topics.topic: Processes and threads counted by the process limit
questions: Exactly which processes or threads count against `process_count`, and is the requested bound for user-created children or for the whole sandbox environment?
Does `process_count` include the sandbox runner itself, only its children, or every process charged to the namespace/user, and are threads included?

judgement.why: This is the same question about which processes and threads count against process_count.

quotes: execute_function: [BEHAVIOR] process_count bounds the tasks of the code alive at once: the runner's main thread counts as the first, every live thread and every process the code forked with os.fork counts with its threads, and bubblewrap's own processes are not counted, so process_count 1 allows code without threads or forks. Process creation other than os.fork — subprocess, os.system, os.posix_spawn, os.posix_spawnp and the os.exec family — is subprocess use and raises in the audit hook as a trap hit (A03 rule 4). The runner's audit hook, on os.fork and on starting a thread, counts the tasks of the environment's proc and, when the new task would exceed process_count, writes a resource hit to the channel and raises, so the execution concludes resource_exhausted even when the code catches the error; the parent's setrlimit, set above process_count by the tasks the runner and bubblewrap need, stays the outer bound, and a creation it refuses is reported the same way (A03 required test 2).
precedent.why: The later sandbox contract defines exactly which threads and processes count and excludes bubblewrap's own processes.

topics.topic: Repository and revision-resolution semantics for manifests
questions: What repository or snapshot mechanism gives `manifest_revision` meaning, and what exact failures occur when the location is not such a repository or the revision is absent?
How is a file at a revision obtained from `manifest_location`, including what repository or snapshot mechanism is required and what happens when the revision cannot be resolved?

judgement.why: This is the same manifest revision storage, resolution and failure-behavior question.

precedent.topic: Storage model and resolution behavior for revision-addressed manifests
quotes:
**The manifest at a revision**: `manifest_location` is a directory inside a
   git repository and `manifest_revision` a commit of it; `bindings` reads
   `<service_id>.json` of that directory at that commit as a git object, never
   from the working tree, so a record changes only with the configured revision
   (A08 rules 1 and 6).

**A manifest that cannot be read at start** in
   `bindings.check_installed_instances`: the start stops and names it; every
   start step is required (State 3, "Start").
precedent.why: The later text defines revision reads as Git-object reads at a commit and makes an unreadable startup manifest stop startup.

topics.topic: Serialization of path-placeholder values, including empty segments
questions: What exact bytes are placed into a URL path for string and integer placeholder values?
What happens when a string placeholder value is empty, producing an empty segment and potentially `//` after substitution?

quotes: prepare_request: [BEHAVIOR] Builds the URL as base_url without one trailing slash followed by the declared path, each placeholder segment replaced by its input value, which must be a non-null string or an integer written in decimal, UTF-8 percent-encoded except the RFC 3986 unreserved characters so that it stays one segment; nothing else in the URL is normalized.

prepare_request: [VALIDATION_ERROR] An input is not placeable, giving input_not_placeable with the port named, when a placeholder value is not a non-null string or integer, or a GET or DELETE query value is not a string, integer, number, boolean, null or list of those; inputs are examined in port name order and a list's elements in list order, and the first that cannot be placed is named; an input placed in the path is placed nowhere else.
judgement.why: The later invocation contract specifies decimal integers and UTF-8 percent encoding and permits every non-null string, including an empty string.

topics.topic: Stable determination of the plain-HTTP loopback exception
questions: How is the loopback exception determined and prevented from changing through DNS resolution or rebinding?

Does this mean only a literal loopback IP, a hostname such as `localhost`, or any hostname whose DNS result is loopback; and when multiple or changing DNS answers exist, which address controls the decision?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about determining which hosts qualify for the loopback exception.

precedent.topic: Definition of hosts covered by the plain-HTTP loopback exception
quotes:
Plain `http` is allowed only for an instance of
   class `local_dev` or `disposable_rig`, as the manifest instance's `class`
   states — an absent or unknown class counts as `production` — or one whose
   `api_base_url` host is a loopback address; any other plain `http` target is refused before sending.
precedent.why: The definition of loopback concerns unchanged text and was not made material by the change.

topics.topic: Stored-value ceiling used for mapped-list results across upgrades
questions: Which release's `stored_value_bytes_max` is used to derive an unfinished or historical mapped node's aggregate result after an upgrade?
Which ceiling is used to derive the result of an existing run after an upgrade, and how can its final status remain stable when the original ceiling is not recorded?

judgement.why: This is the same question about which release ceiling governs mapped-list derivation across upgrades.

precedent.topic: Which release's non-contract ceilings govern historical records and derived mapped failures
quotes: read_value_bytes: [RETURN_SHAPE] Returns the digest-checked bytes exactly as stored.

record_change: [BEHAVIOR] MUST apply the one StoreChange given in one SQLite transaction that either writes every record the variant lists or nothing; it writes no record the variant does not list and trusts the caller for every decision of the caller's rule, checking only its own invariants: attempt numbers, unique and existing identities, existing linked records, and no edit of an immutable record. Records of the kinds that are never edited — issued contract versions, implementations, trial cases, flow versions, values, verdicts, activations and trace records — are only ever written once; for any other entity a lifecycle change — a status, who decided, resolved, revoked, cancelled or released and when, concluded_at, ended_at, waiting points, outputs — updates those fields of the entity's one record in place, and the record keeps its store position, the position of its creation; no other field of a written record ever changes.

advance_run: [SCHEMA_CONSTRAINT] A value port's PortRef names exactly one StoredValue; a mapped node's value output, once every element succeeded, is one StoredValue holding the canonical JSON array of the elements' values in element order, whose value_schema is the canonical array schema with the port's value_schema as items, of the highest class among the elements, an empty list taking the highest class among the node's inputs, the mapped list and every other input, published with put_value_bytes and written by runs when the list is first delivered, never in an element's own change; when its canonical bytes exceed the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant nothing is written and the node is failed for its dependants, which conclude upstream_failed, every element record staying as it is; only a list that is delivered, to a node or a flow output, is measured, and an output no edge takes fails nothing; a mapped node's file output is one SpooledFilesRef listing every element's files in element order, derived from the elements' NodeExecutions whenever it is delivered, after a restart too, since no record of its own holds it, whose disclosure_class is the highest class among the elements, an empty list taking the highest class among the node's inputs, the mapped list and every other input; a mapped element receives the list element at its map_index as its own StoredValue of the map_over port's value_schema and the list's class, or the spooled file at that position.
precedent.why: The later contracts preserve and read durable records unchanged while applying the installed release's imported ceilings whenever new work, including post-restart mapped-list derivation, is performed.

topics.topic: Tie-breaking order for flow hashing and first proof failure
questions: How are tied constants and edges ordered for hashing and for selecting the first proof failure?
How are edges with the same endpoints but different guards, and constants with the same target but different values, ordered for hashing and first-failure selection when the stated sort keys tie?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about tie-breaking for equal edge or constant sort keys.

precedent.topic: Canonical tie-breaking for equal edge or constant sort keys
quotes:
Lists
   whose order carries no meaning are sorted before hashing — ports by
   (`direction`, `name`), nodes by `node_id`, edges in the edge order of A05,
   constants by (`to_node`, `to_port`) — so the same content in another order has
   the same identity; list values themselves keep their order.
precedent.why: The missing tie-breakers were already present in the unchanged identity-ordering rule.

topics.topic: Validity of admission verdicts across kernel releases
questions: Does an admission verdict from an earlier release remain valid after runtime or dependency changes, or must the release/runtime identity participate in verdict validity?

quotes:
Submitting an implementation — new, or equal to an existing one — runs
   admission unless an AdmissionVerdict M08 for that implementation and the
   current corpus digest already exists, in which case that verdict is used.
judgement.why: The unconditional reuse rule makes an existing verdict remain valid for the same implementation and corpus after a release change.
